basis: Skeletal dysplasia and cleft palate define the syndrome; airway malacia occurs in 80-99%; conductive hearing impairment in 3/5. Genital anatomy alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft palate is an explicit defining structural malformation, reported in 80-99%; the palate belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Immune-mediated skeletal muscle disease; interstitial lung disease directly damages lungs in approximately 30-40% overall, with substantial variation by subtype.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: interstitial lung disease occurs in approximately 30-40% across idiopathic inflammatory myopathies and represents direct inflammatory lung injury.

basis: Long QT and syndactyly define classic Timothy syndrome; neurodevelopmental impairment affects ~70-80%; recurrent hypoglycemia affects ~35-40%. Immune dysfunction is less consistently established.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: recurrent hypoglycemia from impaired glucose regulation affects approximately 35-40%, representing intrinsic metabolic dysfunction.

basis: Severe neurodevelopmental disorder; strabismus occurs in 11/11 and ophthalmoplegia in 30-79%; pectus excavatum in 30-79%. Neurogenic feeding difficulties do not establish direct gastrointestinal injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysphagia and feeding difficulties are neurogenic manifestations; direct gastrointestinal tissue damage or intrinsic dysfunction is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: pectus excavatum is a persistent structural skeletal deformity annotated as frequent (30-79%).

basis: Phosphate metabolism disorder with subcutaneous calcific masses; radial bowing reported in 1/1. Nephrocalcinosis in 1/1 lacks demonstrated renal impairment; singleton frequencies remain uncertain.

decisions.renal: none: nephrocalcinosis is reported in 1/1, but impaired renal function or damaging renal consequences of the deposits are not established.

basis: Inherited extracellular pyrophosphate deficiency causes pathological arterial mineralization and cardiac injury. Nephrocalcinosis and hypophosphatemic rickets occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: generalized arterial calcification is an inherited disorder of extracellular pyrophosphate metabolism, independently of occasional hypophosphatemic rickets.

basis: Precursor T-cell malignancy of blood and marrow; direct leukemic hepatic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in approximately 40-60%. A mediastinal thymic mass does not establish lung involvement.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in approximately 40-60%; this is direct occupation by leukemia rather than a separate liver disease.

basis: Familial immune-mediated cutaneous lichen planus; damaging oral involvement in at least 30% of this familial subtype is not established.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: oral involvement estimates from general lichen planus do not establish a frequency of at least 30% in familial lichen planus.

basis: Neutrophil maturation failure causes immunodeficiency; renal hypoplasia and recurrent aphthous mucosal ulceration each occur in 1/1 reported patient. Singleton estimates are uncertain; infections excluded.

decisions.renal: involved: renal hypoplasia is direct structural kidney involvement reported in 1/1; this is the available subtype-specific frequency evidence, with substantial uncertainty.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: recurrent aphthous stomatitis and ulcers occur in 1/1 and represent intrinsic neutropenia-associated mucosal injury; secondary infections are excluded.

basis: Congenital heart defects, particularly VSD, are principal organ manifestations. Skeletal and CNS anomalies are variable, with no established frequency of substantial damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: cloverleaf skull and clinodactyly are variable reported anomalies; neither a defining skeletal disorder nor damaging involvement in at least 30% is established.
